headline: Your agents are outpacing your ability to manage them
summary: This week the bottleneck moved from the models to the people managing them. Vercel says its security agent flagged 57,897 vulnerabilities in its first week, while VulnCheck counted 37,966 findings from Anthropic's Glasswing with only 217 marked fixed. Agents also joined the team: Claude now sits in video calls, Claude Code Projects coordinate parallel threads, and Perplexity says Teammate agent hours grew 11x in a week. They got wallets too, with ChatGPT Wallet letting Dots agents buy things just as United refused unauthorized agents and eBay appeared to shut them out. And the smartest model is not always the best buy: Garry Tan found Fable 5.2 solved slightly fewer coding tasks than Opus 5.5 at 2.8x the cost per solve. Before you add more agents, decide who reviews their work, what they may spend, and which model each task deserves.

threads.title: More bugs than hands
threads.line: Agents find flaws faster than teams can fix them, and attackers move at the same speed. Budget for fixing, not just scanning.

threads.title: The agent joins standup
threads.line: Agents now sit in your calls and shared projects. Someone on your team has to own what they do.

threads.title: Wallets, then walls
threads.line: Agents can now buy, and some sellers are refusing them. Set your policy before your customers' agents show up.

threads.title: Pay for the job, not the badge
threads.line: The newest model can cost more per result. Test cheaper models on each task before upgrading by default.
